source.apa7: Abdoos, B., Di Benedetto, A., & Russo, D. (2025). Integrated design, scale-up, and surrogate-based optimization of PSA systems for hydrogen purification from ammonia decomposition. Chemical Engineering Journal, 526, 170994. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cej.2025.170994
source.read: full text read on 24 November 2026 (15 pages; every table and figure page inspected on the page image). Supplementary material (Table S1 bed sizes for pilot 1, pilot 2, industrial; Figs. S1, S2) NOT read.
source.evidence_grade: modelled (Aspen Adsorption dynamic simulation plus ANN surrogate and NSGA-II); no PSA cycle experiment; model checked against a literature breakthrough curve for a different gas

entries.note: Full NH3 conversion is assumed (advanced catalytic crackers, ref. 25). The feed is an ideal dry binary H2/N2 mixture.

Trace NH3 removal (membranes or commercial adsorbents) is stated to lie beyond the scope of the study. The conclusions list the effect of ammonia traces as future work. The introduction (p. 2, ref. 7) cites a commercial adsorbent that reduces NH3 to ppb after cracking. NH3 is not a model component.
Water is not mentioned. The feed is dry H2/N2.
Zeolite 13X was fitted as well and rejected. The paper describes no bed layering and no NH3 or H2O guard layer.
The density unit is printed as g/m3 (probably g/cm3). Data adapted from Kast 1988 (ref. 33).

entries.unit: Aspen Adsorption extended Langmuir-Freundlich parameters (units not printed)
entries.note: Exponents (E-07, E-05, E-04) were confirmed on the page image. Fit to single-component isotherm data from refs. 43 and 44 (Rother and Fieback 2013; Kim et al. 1995). Fig. 5 gives R2 = 0.997 to 0.999. The 13X parameters are also in Table 7 and are not carried here.

entries.value: 4 adiabatic beds, 8-step cycle (AD, EQ-DP, DP-SP, BD, PU, EQ-RP, RP)
entries.note: One pressure equalisation. Provide-purge from the DP-SP step. Repressurisation with feed gas.

Derived: total cycle 400 s; each bed adsorbs for 100 s (15 + 85 s). Cycle times are NOT decision variables in the optimisation (Table 6), so the step times are assumed to stay fixed for the optimal designs. The paper does not state this explicitly.
Fig. 3 shows about 1 bar during BD and PU. No vacuum step is used.
Not given and not optimised.
The objectives are maximum recovery, maximum purity and minimum SEC. Productivity is reported but is not an objective. NSGA-II: population 400, up to 2500 generations (p. 7).

entries.value: Aspen Adsorption dynamic model: Peng-Robinson, non-isothermal adiabatic, LDF mass transfer, Ergun pressure drop, axial dispersion, 20 upwind nodes
entries.note: Table 2 equations are taken from Yanez et al. 2020 (ref. 32). No mass-transfer coefficient values are printed in the main text.

entries.value: breakthrough (not cyclic PSA) against literature data for H2/N2/CH4/Ar at 1.3e-3 kmol/h, 1 bar, 40 degC
entries.note: Refs. 33 and 45 (Kast 1988; Yanez et al. 2020). The agreement is shown only graphically. The paper notes that a cyclic bed breaks through earlier than a fresh one. The conclusions list experimental validation of the optimised cycles as future work. The model is therefore not independent of Yanez et al. 2020, which the project already uses.

entries.quantity: Surrogate model and its agreement with the full-order model
entries.note: The R2 values are printed on Fig. 13. Figure reading: in the recovery parity plot, points at 72-78 % recovery scatter by about 1-3 percentage points. The paper does not say whether the Table 8 values come from the surrogate or from the full-order model. The surrogate is reported as about 600 times faster (p. 13).

entries.value: feed 60-150 kmol/h (bounds); similarity principle with residence time L/u and particle diameter held constant
entries.operating_point: industrial scale as defined by the authors
entries.note: Bed specifications for pilot 1, pilot 2 and industrial scale are in Supplementary Table S1, which was NOT read.

entries.note: Derived: 2.25 kWh/kg; product H2 about 121.5 kg/h; N2 about 500 ppm. The conclusions (p. 13) describe this point as 'around 99.9 %'.
Derived: 1.78 kWh/kg; product H2 about 105.5 kg/h; N2 about 9,700 ppm.

The SEC of 5.19 MJ/kg is the lowest SEC on the front. It is not the SEC of the 99.99 % design, which is 8.76 MJ/kg (Table 8). Figure reading (Fig. 12): SEC near 5.2 occurs only at purity of about 91-96 %. The 5.19 value is not printed in any table. The earlier search summary 'about 99.99 %, 77 %, 5.2 MJ/kg' combines two different points.
Derived check: 99.03/96.35 = 1.0278 and 6.4/7.2 = 0.8889. Both improvements belong to Optimal design 3 (99.03 %). At 99.99 % the SEC (8.76) is 22 % ABOVE the base case.

entries.operating_point: 'same purity' (up to 99.99 %); 6-7 or 10-12 bar, 60-100 kmol/h, 10-20 or 30-50 degC
entries.note: Recovery for these two designs is not stated. Figure reading (Fig. 12): points near 99.99 % with SEC near 7.8 are coloured about 72-75 % recovery.
Uncertainty about +/-1 point in recovery and +/-0.1 MJ/kg in SEC. The paper keeps purities down to 90 % for high-temperature PEM and SOFC uses (p. 12).

entries.quantity: Recovery on the front at high purity
entries.note: At about 99.99 % the front runs from about 69 % recovery (lower SEC, about 6.5-7.5 MJ/kg) to 77.4 % (Region 1, highest SEC). Points coloured about 84-87 % recovery appear only at purity of about 99.2-99.8 %. Uncertainty: about +/-3 points in recovery (colour scale on a low-resolution image) and about +/-0.1 point in purity. No point at or above 99.9 % is read as exceeding about 82 % recovery.

High-purity points sit near 0.005. Table 8 gives no productivity values. The sensitivity plots disagree with each other on the base-case level (Fig. 7b about 1.6e-2; Fig. 8b about 2.8e-2; Fig. 8d about 2.4e-2; Fig. 8f 1.05e-2 to 2.6e-2). This is an internal inconsistency.

entries.location: derived from p. 13 Table 8 with the binary-feed definition, Eq. 9, p. 6 Table 5
entries.note: N2 = (100 - purity %) x 1e4, because the product holds only H2 and N2. Purity is printed to 2 decimals, so Opt1 is 50-150 ppm. No ppm values are printed in the paper.
NH3 is not modelled.

entries.note: The paper does not mention ISO 14687 or Grade D. It states only that low-temperature PEM fuel cells need high purity (p. 2, p. 12). The only Table 8 point compatible with Grade D for N2 is at 77.44 % recovery.
Fig. 3 shows about 1 bar.

entries.location: derived from p. 13 Table 8 and A01
entries.note: Binary mass balance on 75/25 feed: tail H2 = 0.75(1-R); tail N2 = 0.25 - N2 in product. Tail-gas composition is not printed in the paper and the paper does not discuss tail-gas use.

entries.value: feed-gas compressor work (single adiabatic compression, eta 0.8) per kg H2 product
entries.note: The inlet pressure of the compressor is not printed. Derived reconstruction: compression of the whole feed from 1 bar to P_ads (gamma 1.4, eta 0.8, T_feed) reproduces Table 8 SEC within 1-3 % (base 7.33 vs 7.2; Opt1 8.92 vs 8.76; Opt2 8.31 vs 8.10; Opt3 6.53 vs 6.4). The SEC is therefore essentially feed compression from about atmospheric pressure. It contains no valve or vacuum work and no other PSA power. Text p. 6 gives T in degC in the formula, probably meaning K.

entries.quantity: Sensitivity to adsorption pressure, 6 to 12 bar
entries.note: Uncertainty about +/-0.3 units. Purity rises and recovery falls with pressure (also stated in text p. 8). At 10 bar the curve gives about 93 % purity, not the 96.35 % of the Table 8 base case. The sensitivity reference point is therefore not exactly the Table 8 base case (internal inconsistency or unstated reference).

entries.quantity: Sensitivity to feed temperature, 10 to 50 degC
entries.note: Uncertainty about +/-0.3.

entries.note: Uncertainty about +/-0.5.

entries.quantity: Sensitivity to bed diameter, 0.7 to 1.2 m
entries.note: Uncertainty about +/-0.5. The text (pp. 8, 10) names pressure and bed diameter as the strongest influences on SEC.

entries.quantity: Sensitivity to feed flow, 60 to 150 kmol/h
entries.note: Uncertainty about +/-0.5.

entries.quantity: Sensitivity to purge, cycle time or residual NH3
entries.note: Not studied. Cycle step times are fixed (Table 1).

entries.quantity: Economics of the three optimal designs
entries.note: Aspen Process Economic Analyzer, CEPCI to 'the current year' (p. 7). Operating hours, H2 selling price, cost year, compressor size and the content of 'raw materials' are not stated. Internal inconsistencies: (i) Opt2 sales printed 2.7882 cannot give the printed 4.412 yr payout; the payout implies about 9.78. The text says revenue is similar to Zone 1. (ii) The text calls Zone 1 the highest CAPEX, but Table 9 gives Zone 2 higher (8.6104 > 8.556).

No per-kg purification cost is printed, although the abstract says the purification cost was estimated. Derived, only as an order of magnitude and assuming 8760 h/yr (not stated): Opt1 operating cost 6.926 MUSD/yr over about 864 t/yr is about 8 USD/kg. That figure evidently includes raw materials (feed gas), so the purification-only cost cannot be isolated. Not usable as an AmCraX input.
